title: quest init for a Codex target: write the skill where Codex reads repository skills, and make a non-interactive Windows init say so (ODOC-556)
description: Carrier task for opum-doc ODOC-556, an operator-reported product defect (first-party, 2026-10-31). Operator: on a Windows host with Codex, `quest init` with Codex selected "put the sklll in .quest", and `lore init` prompted for nothing and wrote no skill or managed block. Measured here 2026-10-31 (read, not reproduced on Windows): the skill path is the single constant questSkillPath = ".claude/skills/quest/SKILL.md" (src/application/agents/agent-instructions.ts), written once whenever any instructions were written, for every target, so a Codex-only target gets a Claude path. Nothing in the skill-write path puts a file under .quest/ (LocalAgentInstructionPort resolves against the repo root); the .quest placement is unreproduced, and a plausible misread is .claude\skills\quest. The wizard runs only when stdout AND stdin are TTYs with no flags (src/cli/main.ts ~2185); a Windows host where either is not a TTY (Git Bash/mintty pipes, an IDE terminal) falls to the scripted path and, with no --agent-instructions, writes no bridge and says nothing. Codex repository skills location, current docs (developers.openai.com/codex/skills, redirecting to learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-skills): `$REPO_ROOT/.agents/skills`, scanned from the working directory up to the repository root; a skill is a directory with SKILL.md (name and description required); the docs do not mention .codex/skills. Design (opum-doc, implement as decided): (1) on Windows a bare interactive init runs its wizard in PowerShell, cmd and Windows Terminal at least; where a terminal cannot be detected as interactive, init says so and names the flags instead of silently doing nothing. (2) A Codex target writes its skill where current Codex reads repository skills, verified against Codex docs at build time, same location as lore; never .claude/ for a Codex-only target, never under .quest/. (3) Each fix has a test that runs on a Windows CI runner. lore and quest release as a pair (Article 3). Plan and file list are in the task notes; no branch or code until the leader says GO.

acceptanceCriteria.text: On a Windows host with Codex, a bare interactive quest init runs its wizard and, with Codex selected, writes the skill and the managed block in AGENTS.md

With Codex selected, init writes the skill at the location Codex reads repository skills (.agents/skills/quest/SKILL.md per the docs read 2026-10-31), never under .claude/ for a Codex-only target and never under .quest/, and lore and quest write the same location
A terminal init cannot detect as interactive prints a notice naming the flags instead of silently writing no bridge
Each fix has a test that runs on a Windows CI runner
The fixes ship in a released version, paired with lore-cli (Article 3)

implementationNotes: First-cut plan (not started; waiting for the leader GO and the dispatch floor): (1) per-target skill path: replace the questSkillPath constant with a function of target, codex -> .agents/skills/quest/SKILL.md, claude unchanged, antigravity per its own docs; thread it through writeInitInstructions, quest agents (check/update/force) and drift checks. (2) init wizard: when stdout or stdin is not a TTY and no flags were given, print a notice naming --agent-instructions --target and --skill-source instead of writing nothing; check Windows TTY detection under Bun for PowerShell, cmd and Windows Terminal. (3) migration: a leftover .claude/skills/quest for a Codex-only workspace reports as drift, never auto-deleted. (4) tests: path-per-target unit tests plus a Windows runner leg. Expected files: src/application/agents/agent-instructions.ts, src/cli/main.ts, src/application/command-help.ts, src/application/agents/guides.ts, test files, and a CI workflow (Windows runner leg: .github/workflows/prepublication-qualification.yml or a new one; a DEC-182 path class, so Opus review). Windows runners already exist in prepublication-qualification.yml (windows-2022, windows-11-arm), and projection-platform.yml runs a Windows leg only on tag or dispatch.

OPERATOR CONFIRMATION (first-party, relayed by opum-doc ~01:03Z 2026-10-31): "yes I meant it put in .claude". On Windows the Codex target wrote .claude/skills/quest; nothing wrote under .quest/ (my code reading was right). Design unchanged: .agents/skills for a Codex target. WINDOWS TEST PLACEMENT, leader ruling OPTION D (OPAG-166: platform matrices run on tags and releases only): add the new tests as a step INSIDE the existing win32 legs of immutable-candidates in .github/workflows/prepublication-qualification.yml, under their EXISTING dispatch/tag `if`; no new job, no `if` change, no new action/pin/dependency, source-gates untouched. Evidence: ONE workflow_dispatch of prepublication-qualification.yml on the branch; put the run id and the two win32 results incl. isTTY log lines in the PR body. Pre-cleared floor work; PR gets an Opus review. NOT option A (per-PR job) and NOT B (drop the event condition). My earlier premise that the Windows legs run on PRs was wrong: immutable-candidates has `if: workflow_dispatch || tag`.

REVIEW 2026-10-31: Opus APPROVE at 3437fe80 on PR #698, no blocking items. Fixes made as text only: (1) CHANGELOG scopes "--force does not remove it" to skill_source=repo and states the QCLI-309 orphan path still removes a byte-exact generated .claude skill under plugin/none for a codex target; (2) CHANGELOG drops "unreproduced" for the .quest placement, since the operator confirmed they meant .claude; (3) agents --force help now says a codex target checks both paths. OPEN R1, routed to opum-doc by the leader: whether --force should remove a byte-exact .claude skill for a codex target under plugin/none; behaviour deliberately NOT changed in #698. Difference from lore named in the PR body: quest reports the leftover on --check only, lore also prints it on update.

OPERATOR CHECKLIST, quest half (ODOC-556 criterion 1; lore's half is in LCLI-772). Recorded 2026-10-31 so a renewal does not lose it; the draft was a session scratchpad file. Not sent to the operator and no sitting booked.
Run on a Windows host with Codex installed, once per shell: PowerShell, cmd, Windows Terminal (a real interactive tab, not a redirected one). Fresh empty git repository each time (git init first). Needs quest built from the QCLI-543/545 release. In each, run a bare `quest init` (no flags).
EXPECT: (1) A wizard prompts (name, task id prefix, agent instructions). Select Codex. If NO prompt appears you should instead see on stderr: "quest init: no interactive terminal was detected (stdin is a TTY: X, stdout is a TTY: Y), so the wizard did not run and no agent instructions or skill were written. Re-run in a terminal, or pass the flags: --agent-instructions --target <claude|codex|antigravity> (and --skill-source <repo|plugin|none>)." Record the two true/false values and the shell: that is a failure of criterion 1, with evidence (inside a git repository the workspace is still initialized, exit 0; outside one, init fails with a validation error, exit 6, before the notice). (2) Afterwards exist: .agents/skills/quest/SKILL.md (front matter name: quest) and AGENTS.md with a quest:agent-instructions managed block. (3) Must NOT exist: any SKILL.md under .quest/, a stray .claude/ directory. Tick only Codex in the wizard (it pre-checks nothing); if you tick Claude, .claude/skills/quest/SKILL.md and CLAUDE.md are expected, and ticking Antigravity writes GEMINI.md plus the same .agents/skills/quest/SKILL.md as Codex (QCLI-548, ruling 28b8ed5; nothing under .claude), so record which boxes you ticked. (4) `quest agents --check --target codex`: exit 0. (5) Leftover check: create .claude/skills/quest/SKILL.md by hand, run `quest agents --check --target codex`: exit 6 with the message for the workspace's skill source, then delete the file. Repo mode (the default after the steps above): ".claude/skills/quest/SKILL.md is a leftover: quest now writes its Codex skill to .agents/skills/quest/SKILL.md. Move or delete it by hand; quest never deletes it." In repo mode only, a Quest block in CLAUDE.md exempts it (the path is then in use by a Claude target); a GEMINI.md block alone does not (QCLI-548). For --target antigravity the message reads "... quest now writes its Antigravity skill to ..." (repo mode) and "... an antigravity target reads its skill from ... and this workspace generates none ..." (plugin/none). Under skill source plugin or none (quest init --reconfigure --skill-source plugin|none): ".claude/skills/quest/SKILL.md is a leftover: a codex target reads its skill from .agents/skills/quest/SKILL.md and this workspace generates none. Move or delete it by hand; quest never deletes it, --force included." and a CLAUDE.md block does NOT exempt it. In every mode `quest agents --update-instructions --target codex --force` leaves the file in place (it says nothing about it today: QCLI-546).
Record per shell: prompts shown yes/no, the two files present, no stray files, the exit codes. Difference from lore, on purpose: lore reports its old .codex path whenever it exists; quest stays silent in repo mode only when a Claude target (CLAUDE.md block) is present.
